title: rc-live-6: uncertain hip / shin bone (fresh paraphrase) -> hip -> S$3,750 only

turns.user: My husband Daniel tripped on the stairs at our flat last night. The hospital says it is a closed break - either his hip or his shin bone, the tibia; the scans are not back yet. What would his personal accident cover give him?
turns.visible:
The Group Insurance Benefits Booklet (page 7) pays the Simple Fracture as a percentage of the Simple Fracture Benefit Limit of S$5,000 for each listed case: Skull 100%; Hip 75%; Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee 50%; Arm, Wrist or Elbow 40%. The booklet defines Other Fracture as a fracture that is not a Simple Fracture, including a compound (open) fracture.
Which fracture site do Daniel’s scans confirm: his hip or his lower leg (shin/tibia)?

turns.user: The specialist has just told us it is definitely the hip.
turns.visible: If the Simple Fracture benefit applies to Daniel's case “Hip” (as you described: “it is definitely the hip”), the conditional illustration is S$3,750: 75% of the Simple Fracture benefit limit of S$5,000, under the Group Insurance Benefits Booklet; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision, and only for an injury the insurer accepts as caused by an accident (the policy says “We will pay the percentage of the Simple Fracture Benefit Limit shown below for a Simple Fracture of a nature listed, caused by an Accident”).
